change.content: The existing Aster hub samples every 60 seconds. The proposed change samples every 30 seconds during a heat alert while preserving the normal cadence and existing reader contract.

fields.current_behavior: Normal operation samples at 60-second intervals and exports the same Reading shape to all controllers.
fields.proposed_behavior: An active heat alert samples at 30-second intervals; alert end restores 60 seconds without changing Reading fields or query semantics.

impact.content: The change affects cadence requirement R-SAMPLE-60 and scheduler capacity, but not validation, buffering, data shape, or latest-reading errors.

fields.impacted_items: R-SAMPLE-60, scheduler load, heat-alert state, and the cadence verification case require revision; interface and schema requirements do not.
fields.rationale: Faster heat-response decisions need more samples, while limiting the delta to cadence avoids destabilizing existing consumers.

compatibility.content: Existing controllers see only more frequent values and require no migration. The default remains 60 seconds until an authorized alert is active.

fields.compatibility_constraints: Keep Reading fields, query operation, UTC format, and latest-valid errors unchanged; the heat-alert rate must be optional and disabled by default.
fields.migration_notes: Deploy with alert mode off, enable it per hub through reviewed configuration, and retain 60-second behavior for unconfigured hubs.

acceptance.content: Acceptance compares the old and new cadence in one controlled session and checks that an old controller can parse every response without modification.

fields.measurable_conditions: Alert mode yields 30±0.1-second samples, exit restores 60±0.1 seconds, and all responses retain the original required fields and errors.
fields.verification_method: Demonstrate alert entry/exit with fake time and run the unchanged version 1 controller contract checks.

trace.content: The supplied model declares Example::Sensor as a participant only. Cadence, heat-alert state, Reading and query changes are proposed language-side designs without current SysML realization; the minimal model cannot establish those behaviors.

fields.model_elements: Example::Sensor is the supplied participant. Cadence, heat-alert, Reading and query concepts are proposed language-side design, not declarations in example.sysml.
fields.unresolved_items: Battery impact, alert authorization, and the acceptable sustained alert duration require further review.
